events.subtitle: HOMEWORK / jazz arrangements of Oe's 1980s-90s catalog
events.factual_description: Blue Note Tokyo presents Senri Oe Trio on January 27, 28, and 29, 2027, with sets starting at 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM each day. The announced trio is Oe on piano, Matt Clohesy on bass, and Ross Pederson on drums. The venue frames the engagement around HOMEWORK, Oe's ninth original album and his first in three years, released in June 2026, alongside jazz arrangements of representative songs he originally released during his 1980s-90s singer-songwriter career. Blue Note Tokyo's biography notes that Oe ended his domestic pop activity in 2008, moved to New York to pursue jazz piano, studied at The New School, and subsequently began his jazz career as a leader. The listed music charge is ¥9,900, with additional seat charges for some seating categories.

en.why_it_matters: The interesting part is the collision between Oe's two musical lives. He left a major Japanese singer-songwriter career to rebuild himself in New York as a jazz pianist, and this trio now puts new HOMEWORK material beside jazz arrangements of songs from his own 1980s and 1990s catalog. That makes the repertoire itself a live argument about reinvention: the same songwriter revisiting earlier melodic DNA through piano-trio language rather than simply performing a nostalgia set.
en.trip_verdict: If January 27-29 overlaps a Tokyo stay, attend if one of the six sets fits naturally around stronger anchors. Three nights provide ample flexibility, so use Aoyama as a smart evening option rather than reorganizing the trip around a scarce opportunity.

es.why_it_matters: Lo interesante es el choque entre las dos vidas musicales de Oe. Dejó una carrera importante como cantautor japonés para reconstruirse en Nueva York como pianista de jazz, y ahora este trío pone material nuevo de HOMEWORK junto a arreglos de jazz de canciones de su propio catálogo de los años ochenta y noventa. El repertorio mismo se vuelve así un argumento en vivo sobre reinvención: el mismo compositor revisitando su ADN melódico anterior desde el lenguaje del piano trío, no simplemente montando una noche de nostalgia.
es.trip_verdict: Si del 27 al 29 de enero coincide con una estancia en Tokio, iría a uno de los seis sets si embona naturalmente alrededor de anclas más fuertes. Tres noches dan bastante flexibilidad, así que usaría Aoyama como una muy buena opción de noche sin reorganizar el viaje alrededor de una oportunidad escasa.

events.subtitle: Sketches of Miles — Miles Davis centennial program
events.category: Miles Davis centennial / all-leader quintet / special repertoire presentation
events.factual_description: Keystone Korner Baltimore presents ARTEMIS: Sketches of Miles on Friday and Saturday, December 11-12, 2026, with sets at 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM both nights. The announced quintet is Renee Rosnes on piano and keyboards, Ingrid Jensen on trumpet, Nicole Glover on tenor saxophone, Noriko Ueda on bass, and Allison Miller on drums. Keystone Korner and its authorized InstantSeats listing frame the program specifically around the centennial of Miles Davis's birth and the endurance of his musical innovations. Rosnes's official performance schedule separately labels the Baltimore engagement a 'Special presentation: Sketches of Miles.' Live tickets are listed at $45-$55 before fees; a $15 streaming pass is also offered.

en.why_it_matters: This is not simply an ARTEMIS booking with a centennial label pasted on it. Rosnes, Jensen, Glover, Ueda and Miller are all strong compositional and improvisational voices, and the stated live premise is to test Miles Davis's continuing influence through a current quintet whose own music already depends on elasticity, space and rhythm-forward interaction. The trumpet-centered lineage matters, but so does hearing five contemporary bandleaders decide what in Miles still generates new ensemble behavior rather than museum reverence.
en.trip_verdict: From the DMV, actively make room for one of the four Baltimore sets; the short trip is justified by the program-specific framing and this exact quintet. If coming from farther along the corridor, pair it with another Baltimore or DC-area reason rather than treating it as a stand-alone long-haul mission.

Rosnes, Jensen, Glover, Ueda y Miller son voces fuertes como compositoras e improvisadoras, y el argumento explícito del concierto es poner a prueba la vigencia de Miles Davis desde un quinteto actual cuya propia música depende de elasticidad, espacio e interacción rítmica. La línea de la trompeta importa, pero también escuchar a cinco bandleaders contemporáneas decidir qué parte de Miles todavía provoca comportamiento nuevo dentro del ensamble en vez de reverencia de museo.
es.trip_verdict: Desde el DMV, sí le haría espacio activamente a uno de los cuatro sets en Baltimore; el short trip se justifica por el programa específico y por esta formación exacta.
